title: How to Rebuild a Toilet Tank: Replacing Fill and Flush Valves (This Old House)
summary: This Old House presents a step-by-step, tool-agnostic repair guide for diagnosing and fixing a leaking or constantly running toilet by rebuilding the tank internals. The host explains the tank anatomy (flapper/flush valve, fill valve, and float) and contrasts older copper floats with modern plastic/embedded floats. The segment identifies common leak scenarios (running toilet, overfill,-condensation nuances) and then demonstrates a complete tank rebuild: shutting off water, draining the tank, disconnecting the supply line, removing bolts, and replacing both the fill and flush valves with a universal kit priced around $20. Finally, it covers reassembly, adjusting the refill height and float, and verifying proper operation, including cautions against overtightening and ensuring the overflow height is correctly set to prevent spills.

sections.title: Anatomy of the Toilet Tank and Core Functions
sections.description: Introduces the tank's two essential tasks: flushing water out via the flapper/flush valve and refilling the tank via the fill valve, with the float regulating shutoff. Explains the path water takes from tank to bowl and contrasts older copper floats with modern plastic/embedded floats.

sections.title: Common Leaks and Running-Toilet Diagnoses
sections.description: Details how a toilet can run continuously when the flapper doesn’t seal properly or the fill valve is misadjusted, causing water to overflow or run into the bowl. Discusses the role of the overflow tube and signs of external leakage (condensation vs. actual water loss).

sections.title: Preparation: Isolating Water and Draining the Tank
sections.description: Shows how to shut off the water supply, flush to empty the tank, and prepare to disconnect the supply line, including practical tips for handling residual water with a turkey baster or wet vac.

sections.title: Disassembly: Removing Old Valves and Bolts
sections.description: Demonstrates loosening and removing the mounting bolts and old valve hardware from the toilet tank, identifying the potential leak points (three bolts, fill/flush valve, spud area).

sections.title: Installing a Universal Valve Kit
sections.description: Introduces a complete valve kit and explains its components, including an adjustable fill valve and a replaceable flush valve, designed to fit multiple tank sizes. Notes approximate cost (~$20) and the benefit of replacing multiple wear points at once.

sections.title: Reassembly, Adjustment, and First Test
sections.description: Guides reinstalling the tank, tightening bolts with care to avoid cracking, seating the spud gasket, aligning the refill tube with the overflow, setting the refill height just below the overflow, and finally adjusting the float to achieve the correct water level. Ends with a practical nod to verifying operation.
